holidays.name: National Grilled Cheese Sandwich Day
holidays.description: A salute to the gooey, golden, butter-crisped comfort classic. Today is the day to pull out the skillet, pick your cheese, and decide whether tomato soup is a requirement or merely a very good idea.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance that grew out of America's long love affair with the melty sandwich. Its exact founder is unclear.
holidays.funFact: Grilled cheese took off in the 1920s, when affordable sliced bread and processed cheese became widely available. Its popularity grew further when the open-faced version was served to schoolchildren and sailors.

holidays.name: Yuri's Night
holidays.description: A worldwide party celebrating space exploration. People gather for cosmic-themed gatherings, star-gazing, music, and science events in honor of humanity's journey beyond Earth.
holidays.origin: It marks two spaceflight milestones on April 12. In 1961, Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space. In 1981, the first Space Shuttle, Columbia, launched. The celebration began in 2001 and has grown into events held in many countries.
holidays.funFact: Gagarin's orbit around Earth lasted only about 108 minutes. The first Yuri's Night parties were held in 2001, the 40th anniversary of his flight.

holidays.name: Walk on Your Wild Side Day
holidays.description: A playful invitation to break out of your routine. Try a bold outfit, take a different route, or order something new off the menu. Today is for doing something a little out of character.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin.
holidays.funFact: The name nods to the Lou Reed song "Walk on the Wild Side," which made that phrase a popular way to talk about adventurous living.
